<term>Picatrix on Magic</term> <note>A significant work on celestial magic.</note>, <term>sorcery</term> <note>original French: "sortilege"; refers to divination or the casting of lots/spells.</note>, 15th century, Library of the Church of Paris

<summary>This is the title page of a 15th-century Latin manuscript of the Picatrix, a famous manual of astral magic, formerly held in the library of Notre-Dame de Paris.</summary>
<keywords>Picatrix, astrological magic, grimoire, 15th century, Notre-Dame de Paris, sorcery, celestial formation</keywords>

--- Page 3 ---
<meta>This page continues the introduction to the manuscript known as the *Picatrix*. While the previous page provided the archival context from the Library of the Church of Paris, this page begins the formal text of the work itself, starting with a traditional religious invocation and a historical account of the book's translation from Arabic into Spanish under the patronage of King Alfonso X "the Wise."</meta>

To the praise and glory of the Most High and Almighty God, whose nature it is to reveal Himself to those He has predestined, and also for the enlightenment of Latin scholars who have suffered from a lack of books published by the ancient philosophers: the most illustrious Alfonso, King of the Spains and of all Andalusia <note>original: "Bandalucie." This refers to Al-Andalus, the regions of the Iberian Peninsula under Muslim rule, which Alfonso was in the process of conquering or governing.</note>, commanded with the greatest study and the highest diligence that this book be translated from Arabic into Spanish. Its name is **Picatrix** <note>The name *Picatrix* is thought to be a Latinization of the Arabic name "Buqratis" (Hippocrates) or a corruption of the name of the original author, Maslama al-Majriti.</note>. I, however, have brought this work to completion in the year of our Lord 1475 <unclear>Alexandr phj s b m Caesar 1465</unclear> at the altars of <unclear>un de lo Capeoni</unclear>, which was compiled by many noble and honored men through the reading of this book out of 200 books and more <unclear>p[...]</unclear>. They called it by its own name; but the King received it under the name *Picatrix*, a book which the most wise <unclear>p[...]</unclear> Picatrix composed from many books concerning the arts of <term>necromancy</term> <note>original: "nigromantiaria." In the Middle Ages, this term was often used broadly to describe "astrological magic" or the summoning of spirits, rather than strictly "communication with the dead."</note>.

---

<margin><image-desc>A vertical decorative flourish or border element resembling a stylized vine with leaves, marking the start of the new section.</image-desc></margin>

And it is the first thing a wise man ought to do in all our affairs: to **give thanks to God**. Because of this, I say—and let the Praised One be my witness—that under His light, holy things are revealed and hidden things are made manifest. By His power, all things known were made, and in Him all skilled men and all branches of knowledge are reckoned. Rightly, by His mercy, they belong to Him; and through that same mercy, by devotion and intellect, all created things have been formed and brought to their end. By His power, all things are called forth, renewed, and established in their nature, and are governed according to their merit. Through Him, rather, all things are changed through generation. He is not entangled with other things, nor is He separated from them by having a limited place, nor is He <unclear/>; for He Himself is the very Place of all things. I cannot fully describe all the eminence of the world <unclear/> as His powers flow into all things infinitely. There is nothing in the light of the world unless it be the Praised One Himself. The kingdoms are obedient and stand immovably in the holy ones who have delighted in His commands and in the prophets.

<meta>This page follows the introductory history of the Picatrix's translation from Arabic into Spanish. Having established the book's royal pedigree and its purpose as a repository of ancient wisdom, the author now transitions into the metaphysical framework of the work and a detailed table of contents for the upcoming sections.</meta>

... sciences and other wisdoms, for which we pray to Him that He may lead us into His grace and mercy toward His eternal glory. Amen.

->O you who know the intention of the <term>spheres</term> <note>The celestial spheres which, in medieval cosmology, were believed to surround the Earth and influence terrestrial events.</note> through divine wisdom and as a true inspirer, grant to those of us who have set out to prepare and understand certain parts of the invisible currents—moving more toward the heights—an invisible and great reason, eternal and without stain. First, however, one ought to know through this science about the philosophical veils and the descriptions of honors in which it leads us, and the Overseer <note>original: "uisitatorem." This likely refers to a spiritual guide or an advanced practitioner.</note> within. Then, whatever they were speaking of in it <unclear>your</unclear> <unclear>unless</unclear> by signs and likenesses, just as they are held; Paul speaks of them <note>A reference to St. Paul’s writing, likely regarding the idea of seeing "through a glass, darkly" (1 Corinthians 13:12).</note> and <unclear>it is permitted</unclear> they did so for their ignorant neighbors in words, because if this science were exposed to men, they would confound all things and these spiritual matters of the <unclear>rising</unclear> would perish. They do this so that no one may be able to reach it unless there were a supreme illumination from Him, and from those things in all their likenesses of life, <unclear>that is</unclear> and the <unclear>sparks</unclear> by which the wise may be able to reach it surely in the virtues which are willed by God in truth. Therefore, and for this cause, we have compiled this book in which wisdom is made plain. I intend to gloss the brief path of this discourse and the speech which the wise have spoken. And to show that which they revealed in their books to you through the knowledge of God, called <unclear>lombis</unclear>. I, however, pray to the Most High that this our book should not come but into the hands of a wise man who can understand whatever we have said within it, and that he may hold it in good, and whatever he shall work may be for the good, according to the state of God, as is necessary.<-

<margin>Division of the book</margin>
Moreover, this work is divided into four books, each of which is divided into its own parts. In the **first book**, it treats of the nature of the orb and its single effect through the proper <term>images</term> <note>original: "ymagines." In this context, these are astrological talismans or symbols designed to capture the influence of the stars.</note> which are in it. For the form, it speaks of the qualities and figures of the orb through the movement of the <term>eighth sphere</term> <note>The sphere of the fixed stars, situated beyond the seven planetary spheres.</note> or concerning the effects in this world. In the total, it speaks of the proportions of the planets and the signs, and I show their figures and forms in their proper color, through the qualities of all the spirits of the planets and the bodies which each possesses, because the first is the master of the others. In the **fourth book** <note>The text here jumps from the first to the fourth book in this summary paragraph.</note>, truly it treats of the proportions of the spirits, namely—

<column-break/>

—those things which must be observed as necessary in this art, or how we are directed in images and <term>suffumigations</term> <note>The ritual burning of incense or other materials to produce smoke, intended to attract or appease planetary spirits.</note> through this matter. The chapters of the first book follow:

The **first chapter** is concerning the manner of knowing in what degree it is.
The **second chapter** <note>The OCR lists "Eorum capitula" and "Capitulum secundum" somewhat redundantly.</note> is what is greater and lesser in property.
The **third chapter** is what the sky is and of what movements it consists.
The **fourth chapter** is concerning the noble proportions and their composition for the forms of the image.
The **fifth chapter** is concerning examples of proportions and what they require for the making of images.
The **sixth chapter** is in what degree things exist in the world and their quality, just as how the <term>microcosm</term> <note>original: "minor mundus." The concept that the human being is a small-scale reflection of the entire universe.</note> is through the <term>macrocosm</term> <note>original: "maiorem mundum." The great world or the universe as a whole.</note> and its likeness.
The **seventh chapter** is in what degree the world is, and concerning many other profound things for the likeness of the wise, which we intend in this his book of wisdom.

---

### Chapter One: Concerning Divine Knowledge, in what degree it may be.

<margin>and one single unity</margin>
Know, then, dearest brother, that the great and noble Lord gave to men the <unclear>gift</unclear> of the world as a fountain, because through it we shall have knowledge of hidden things and what the causes of all things of this world are. And those which pass most closely are the causes of other things and qualities; one thing holds agreement with another. Because of this, the science of all things which exist in any degree is a quality, one thing after another in an elevated way in the <unclear>sight</unclear>, and in which place. He who is the root and principle of all this world, how He is in Himself a single unity beyond definition, and He Himself knows all things by an eternal will. For He is first and greatest in goodness. In Him nothing is lacking, nor does He require any other thing; nor does He Himself cease or depend upon another, just as a table set by itself, nor does He receive quality from another. He is not a body, nor is He composed of any body, nor does He have <unclear>bodies</unclear> with any other, but is entirely through Himself. In the Son, I say, the mind cannot <unclear>think</unclear>, and He is one truth above all truth. And through His unity, He possesses goodness in every way. And because He is pure truth, He requires the truth of no one else, which man <unclear>receives</unclear> from Him.

<meta>This page continues the philosophical and cosmological introduction to the Picatrix. Having established God as the source of all wisdom on the previous page, the author now defines the relationship between the Creator, the cycles of the natural world (generation and corruption), and the human spirit's role in understanding this order through study. This serves as the theoretical foundation for the practical magic defined in Chapter 2.</meta>

All things, since they are approved by God (for He alone is properly God)—neither truth nor form <note>In the Aristotelian sense, "form" is the essential nature or "blueprint" of a thing.</note> exist apart from Him; He is our highest virtue. Furthermore, the goodness of God cannot be perfect in all things [without Him]. Indeed, all things are beneath Him, and from Him they receive their goodness, their generation, and their corruption <note>The phrase "generation and corruption" refers to the natural cycle of birth/growth and decay/death that governs all matter in the physical world.</note> as if from their own cause.
<margin>in parts</margin>
And let it be known here, as much as possible, how each thing properly proceeds from God and from the things themselves; and how He alone precedes Himself <note>Likely referring to God's existence as the "Unmoved Mover" or First Cause.</note> through the order and degree of generation and corruption—all which is called [existence] when one is placed without another. And in what manner those things which are "later" <note>Inferior or subordinate things in the cosmic hierarchy.</note> are the cause of those principal things, and how they themselves are the greatest mysteries in generation in any thing. And in what manner they have their reception, and how they themselves are the cause of the corruption of all things generated under them. And the first of all things is the cause of the corruption and generation of all other things subsisting under it. And that more or less from
<margin>in itself</margin>
the property of God Himself, and so it is mixed in our generation and corruption, not according to any other property, but according to the strength of the order of the three <note>This may refer to the "three worlds" (intellectual, celestial, and elemental) common in occult philosophy.</note> by which all our "later" things are compared to the other. Regarding these common things, we have [the following]. And also in what manner, from the first things of the science of God, all subsequent things have their order through community. He alone is the most high, because by His own property He is detached [from all things]. And know that He is the most high God within us. And everyone ought to study and remain in the mandate of God; for in goodness there is love, science, sense, and goodness proceeds from Him. And the spirit itself is a mobile and high light. And because the student intends to serve God, he ought to observe this world, which holds no forms [of its own], and mostly give heed to its fragility. And from Him, as if from a higher world, the spirit of man descends; in this desire, he ought to run toward the Highest with devotion, studying to discern more clearly through all his writings what kind of world this is and what the "effecting things" <note>The active forces or causes that shape reality.</note> are, and how they do not proceed from us. And the second cause is itself good wisdom. And the things are diverse; He is the maker and caller of the whole world, and of all generated things.
<margin>existence</margin>
And the world itself is named as a gift of God from the Most High; it has been called so, and the satisfaction of man is exceedingly profound and strong to comprehend. Thus, it cannot be comprehended except by study and the science that is held. And this is the greatest gift which the Lord Himself gave to men: to serve through study in thought. For through study, man is [brought] to God. And many things concerning Him, through the property of the earth, are placed as an argument taken from the smallest things. The second is that by which he is elevated in the world of the fourfold forms <note>Referring to the four elements: Fire, Air, Water, and Earth.</note>; which, when taken, appears through things that are hidden. And so he has three strengths, of which the first is what was

<column-break/>

from the prior God [concerning] the man of the world. The second is through the argument of the good movement of the gift, which does not exist for the sake of desire in itself, but he wishes to be chosen and he finds in it the will of all stations. Now, regarding the things through which it is served, we intend to speak of the freedom of his choices and their revelation; it is not except through every argument that he intends to serve as a reasoner. He ought to study in the science of things ordered through perfection. For a man cannot have these services except through wisdom and a student in the ordered science. This is the good of the proverb: "Greatest is the greatness of the gratitude of the one who can help in so many ways."

### Chapter 2: What magic is and what a magician is

Let him who is named in this science know that we call "magic" a magic power. It is everything that man operates and from which he attains sense and form in that work through all parts. And for the sake of the movable things which we use, let it follow through the senses toward wondering <note>Magic is defined here as producing "wonder" (miranda) or effects that amaze the senses.</note>; and these are said to be difficult for the intellect, by reason of the sense which is hidden in similarities. And this is because they are powerful gifts placed for things, for the sake of friendship to the aforesaid. And this science is exceedingly profound and strong for the intellect. And it is placed to move a part of man by its own properties, which the Lord operates from spirit into spirit. And this is in making similar things which are not the various things of the world; and the image is composed of spirit in body, or the most high composition is body in body. And generally, we call "magic" all things hidden from the sense and which very few men apprehend: how it is done or for what causes they divine. And wise men call images <term>telesm</term> <note>original: "telesm." From the Greek *telesma*, this refers to what we now call a "talisman"—a physical object consecrated under specific astrological conditions to hold spiritual power.</note>, which is interpreted as "veiler" <note>original: "uelator." This suggests the talisman "veils" or contains a spiritual force within a physical shell.</note>, because whatever it does, it does primarily through the will. In predicting, it will do that for which it was composed, through the power of the spheres and by appropriate proportions, and by the speeds of the visible [planets] they are composed in their own bodies to fulfill the aforesaid. And this [is done] in opportune times, and with <term>suffumigations</term> <note>The ritual burning of incense or herbs to attract specific planetary or spiritual energies to the talisman.</note> by which the strongest spirits are drawn to the images themselves. And this is, so to speak, an assimilation which moves bodies by altering them from unworthy things toward other cleaner bodies. And they were in images, which all [things]...

they preserve through force, and it works similarly in the process of dissolving bodies: altering them according to nature because the body is a mixture of another body by the power of composition existing within itself. It stands that this property is loosened by which it is composed of two keys <note>original: "clavis"; likely referring to the two "keys" or fundamental components of a chemical or magical compound.</note>, and yet it burns with fire and water. And this fourfold strength is wondered at and is bounded by its own proportion and nature, because it is loosened when it enters and penetrates into any body; it opens its jaws so that the other may be more altered and more easily obey under the transmutable governance. And you shall similarly choose this <term>Elixir</term><note>original: "eligeris"; a common medieval spelling variation of elixir.</note> in the highest manifestation, because it lightly mixes bodies from their own nature into another more noble one, first by evaporating the spirit, then releasing it, and again by taking the seeds that are seen; and when this is finished, you shall choose to follow the ancient sages. 

And this name "Elixir" <note>original: "elisum"</note> is interpreted as a strength like no other, namely a strength that breaks through mixing, and even transmutes from one property to another, until it reduces them to its own likeness. Then, there can be no composition except that of animals, trees or vegetables, and minerals through these parts of composition, just as we have said. Likewise, we know that from the likeness of the world, the world itself is likened to these composite things we have mentioned. And similarly, the Elixir must be composed of these same things. Because as long as one appears, one remains in the other and one enters into the other; for this reason, trees cannot stand by themselves through the vegetative way, nor can animals stand without vegetables and the seed of the other, to create generation there from the fire and the moisture of the air: and then this which is written in the book called the *Book of Orders* is fulfilled.

### The Book of the Orders of Alchemy

Now, however, let us return to our purpose, and I say that <term>Magic</term><note>original: "magis"; likely a scribal error for "magia".</note> is divided into two parts: namely, into science (Theory) and Practice. <term>Theory</term> is the knowledge of the places of the fixed stars, which I have composed regarding the celestial signs and the firmament, and when they have their progression in the planets thus moving toward one another; indeed, the signs are what make us intend that which we know, so that in this we might comprehend all that the ancient sages said and declared regarding the hours and the time for the Great Work <note>A common term for the process of creating the Philosopher's Stone or the ultimate magical goal.</note>. And he who knows this, knows the science of magic and its great power, which consists entirely in the <term>selections</term><note>original: "elixionibus"; likely "elections," the astrological practice of choosing the right time for an action.</note> of hours and times, to be obtained through

<column-break/>

the constellations and motions—the things upon which the master is founded. And also, words are part of magic because they have work to do in it. As <term>Plato</term> says, just as all animals would be valued as nothing if the void <note>Referring to the horror vacui or the essential spirit that fills the world.</note> were imminent, so man falls into wonder when the spirit is emitted, and it appears that a certain part has a greater power within it. And the greatest strength is found when many strengths are joined together; this is the inspection of the power of magic, and this is Theory.

<term>Practice</term>, however, is the composition of these natures, the mixing of the stars by the infusion of the fixed stars; and this science is called "the virtues remaining in one essence." For in this way, every virtue is proven against the other. After all these things have been fundamentally gathered together, those which have the predicted virtues ought to have the value of <term>cements</term><note>original: "cementarum"; materials used to bond or purify metals in alchemy.</note>, and this is for the "passimation" <note>likely "passivatio" or preparation of a surface</note>, which helps in completing this virtue into a finished state. And it must similarly have a natural value for mixing. And this complete light is not possible, nor can they exist without their own seed in animals; and this magic is acquired from the world through arts and works in a different kind of subtlety.

Those things which are acquired by arts and works are learned from masters, which requires a wise mind and good intellect. And the wisdom of which I spoke in the *Book of the Alphabet* <note>original: "libro d'alphabetari"; likely a reference to a specific Hermetic or magical primer.</note> is the same as that spoken of in other books. In which it is said that you should take four years and six <unclear>peros</unclear>; that which is acquired by subtlety and works is what the sages themselves perform, he who worked in the motions of the "made name" <note>Possibly a reference to the Shem HaMephorash or a specific word of power.</note>. We sages also name it thereafter; and these are the sages who also spoke in the aforementioned book. The ancient sages worked with four virtues and subtleties against Alexander <note>Referring to Alexander the Great, often a character in Hermetic lore as a student of Aristotle.</note> in the second [book] regarding those things which are near us. They called this science the "Law of Man," which is interpreted as the "Height of the Spirit of the Heavens." And we do not apply this to all parts of magic. We do not have the power to reach that science itself except through <term>Astrology</term>, so that you do not become such that you are cut off from astrology, since they have a mutual service to the signs. In the eighth sphere, you possess the knowledge of their motions and of the other stars. Thereafter, one must declare the signs in their degrees and their nature and the quality of those signs, so that one of them (the signs) might be seen in the things of the world and in the part of all the planets. One must inspect the twelve signs and the times of the months, and also consider the planets every day and night.

...of the head and tail of the dragon <note>original: "capitis et caude draconis"; the North and South Nodes of the Moon, where its orbit intersects the ecliptic, often associated with destiny and karmic balance in astrology.</note> and good positions in the heavens and all the designations of the signs. In the teaching of the world and the habit of each entity mentioned above, for themselves and for others, because of their designations which are the givers and helpers in knowing which of the planets dominates a figure, and in knowing their order in that dominion; so that one may know these parts of the planets in the zodiac. Without these things, no one can arrive at the work of this science, and all these things are found in the book of astronomy. And through this, we can follow the wise man who spoke in the book of Ptolemy <note>original: "ptolomeo"; likely referring to the *Tetrabiblos* or the *Almagest* by Claudius Ptolemy, the foundational texts for medieval astronomy and astrology.</note> regarding the stones; but the aforementioned heavens must be kept in mind until you know all their movements with their qualities through all thought and sense. And this is what they say when I mention the space of the wine; in another place, it says all life comes from the highest sense and intellect, or we have placed it toward its other parts.

### Chapter Three: What the Heaven is and its Nature

The form of the heaven is spherical, round, and equal on its surface, and thus all things that are within it are equal in their qualities, operations, and movements. And some have thought that the heaven appears not to be round for a time; yet in its qualities, it is certain that the form of the heaven is its own proper form and cannot be otherwise. This is because it is a spiritual form, as one might say in physics, and because that which is first and ancient in the world must undoubtedly possess the most complete form. Furthermore, the complete figure and form is the round or spherical figure, in which all other figures are contained. It is a single general line and a single continuity in the conception of the bodies of the world; so it is with the heaven. No part of the heaven can be outside of the world in the processes of generation and corruption <note>The Aristotelian concept that everything below the moon is subject to birth and decay (generation and corruption), while the heavens are eternal.</note>. For the heaven is like a supreme round sphere in all its parts, perfectly equal in its roundness, and most singularly contained in the world; there is nothing from which all lines drawn to that line are not equal. The point lies in the center and is called the [center of the world], and we designate the givers that the sun <note>original: "phebe"; a poetic term for the sun or radiant light.</note> reaches in the world. And the center is like our own, great and central. In this way, the operations in the divine heaven wish to see a round sphere, encompassing the whole world in its height; it is fitting that such a sphere holds every habitation of its whole place, where the spirits and living creatures could live according to the figures of the stars above.

<column-break/>

Since in every movement there is speculation from itself, with every author's subtle contraction. In the nature of the heaven, there is one nature, and all movements of bodies follow the movement of the heaven. All the heat of this sun and its intuition, and whatever happens in the world, occurs through its qualities. The signs of the heaven are like an eternal dominion, and the figures are to be observed. Because of all this, the judgments of astrology are divided, following the great images of the heaven. The heaven is the cause of all operations of the higher things; the works and portents are many in these things, as are the aspects and conjunctions <note>The geometric relationships (aspects) and alignments (conjunctions) between planets that determine their astrological influence.</note> which they have from the light. Each one holds its own mandates according to the works of the planets which they have in the earthly days. In the world, there are good mansions <note>Refers to the Lunar Mansions, a division of the sky into 28 sections based on the moon's daily progress.</note> for those who would be monastic astronomers, who are also physicians and philosophers. And if Jupiter is present, it is temperate and moist; and if Mars, it is hot and dry. Then there are clear days <note>original: "dies mīdira albus"; likely referring to the 'white' or auspicious quality of the Sun.</note> because of great purity. Regarding the moon <note>original: "Luna"</note>, it is cold and moist. And if they are moved by power, they are divided near the Moon. In some cases, lead <note>Lead is the metal traditionally associated with the planet Saturn.</note> will be of some degree of Venus <note>original: "veni"</note>; that which they have afterward when the planet itself is strong in its mansion, or weak in moisture and dryness. ### Chapter Three: What the Heaven is and its Matter

The form of the heaven is spherical, round, and equal in its surface, so that it may be like all things that exist in the whole of its qualities, operations, and movements. And though some think that the heaven does not appear round at all times, it is certain in its qualities that its form is its own proper shape from which it cannot deviate. It is a <unclear>spiritual</unclear> form, as if to say it is full. From antiquity in this world, that which is first and ancient must have a complete form; and the form and figure that is most complete is the circle, because it is the first of all figures. It is closed by a single line so that nothing may be hindered <gloss>in the decay</gloss> of the bodies of the world that can exist in heaven. Furthermore, no part of heaven can exist in the "world of generation and corruption" <note>original: "generationibus et corruptionibus"; a standard medieval term for the earthly realm where things are born and die, unlike the eternal heavens.</note> in its own essence, and this can only be understood through illumination. It is because the heaven is said to be a round sphere in all its parts, and equal in its humidity, and contained as one in a single point. This point is the center from which all lines drawn to the circumference are equal; this uniform point is where the lines signify the **rays** <term>radii: the astrological influence or "light" projected by stars onto the Earth</term> which those stars extend into the world. And therefore, this is the work, virtue, and greatness, and in this way they operate in this divine governance. The vision of the sphere is total in itself, just as the world is said to be in its substance. Such a virtue has foreknowledge or a place—that is, the figure remained within itself, and from it comes the power of spirits, the mind, and the rest of the fixed stars.

All motion of bodies does not follow the motion of the heaven alone. Every heat, such as that of the sun, is not of itself but through its placement and whatever exists in that manner. For this reason, the degrees of the heaven are marked, even in a small amount of matter, and they appear to be shaped. Because of them, all the judgments of **astrology** are divided, for these judgments follow the "images" <note>original: "ymagines"; referring to the constellations or the symbolic forms of the zodiac.</note> of heaven. They are the cause of every subsequent operation. One can operate and have power because there are many aspects and conjunctions which the stars have with one another, as they are members distant from the work of the planets which have influence over earthly things. In the world, things do not remain static; if an astronomer observes those stars that are cold and dry, or the opposite which are moist, or those that are more hot and dry, then they appear to be of a medium color due to great humidity. Some are lacking, which is to say they are effective due to great dryness. Therefore, the **Moon** is of a cold and moist time. # An image for catching many fish

<margin>Note on catching fish</margin>
Make an **image** <note>original: "ymaginem"; a physical talisman or effigy imbued with planetary power.</note> in the form of a fish, positioned in the river alone while the fish are rising, with **Jupiter** <note>In traditional astrology, Jupiter is the "Great Benefic," associated with growth, abundance, and success.</note> in the **ascendant** <note>The zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of the ritual.</note>. If the hour is favorable in this manner, follow this method: first, take hold of and look into the body [of the image], and after the whole image has been made in the predicted hour, you shall take a fine silver thread. Place the image at the head of the thread in the mouth of a hook. Then, according to another mentioned method, let it have a weight made of lead, and place the said thread and the image in the middle [of the water] for the fish. Let it be filled with water as it happens, and in all places, let the water be preserved as I shall give. Afterward, cast these things into the deep river, and it is said that all the fish that are in that part [of the river] will be caught.

# Chapter Six: In which it is asked who is the
# knower and the quality of the knower; that man is a 
# lesser world and is likened to the greater world.

Know that knowledge, though noble and high, allows those who study it to work toward their own nobility and height. Knowledge is like its own rank, because to know "two" as a stable state appears as something else; <note>This likely refers to the binary of the knower and the known, or the dual nature of man.</note> and this is the perfect man who finds joy in honor. All those who are studious of this pursue it and love it; such people are called **philosophers** in speech—not as ones who are despised, but as lovers [of wisdom]. He who does not labor in this possesses knowledge in name only. For knowledge is the form of the human body. And if this is true, then knowledge is superior to that through which he knows himself as a man: namely, that man himself is a **lesser world** <note>original: "minor mundus"; the concept of the Microcosm.</note> and is similar to the **greater world** <note>original: "maior mundus"; the Macrocosm, or the universe.</note>. He is a body completed with his own rational soul. And he is separated from all other similar things, such as the animals of the world. It is most just that man, who is accustomed to being rational and is governed by it, should be able to apprehend truth through himself, to discern those things which are not, to intend toward those which are in the world, and to grasp them in whatever place they exist. And so it would be, as it is said, that by his power he might see this within himself: that he can consider the judgment of forms. Regarding the **lesser world**, it is the same as and similar to the **greater world**, which it assimilates in its form and its likenesses. This is true as it is with animals in all natural things, but man is separated from animals in his **masteries** <note>technical skills or crafts</note> and sciences. He possesses existence through motions, as all things are naturally ordered in a straight line through open movements.

For he has fingers and palms with a certain composition; he has a round head, and roundness through the body of women, and the forehead, and the summit of mastery. He has teeth and all other things arranged in opposition, and he has flat surfaces; just as he speaks, so he knows how to weep. He acts and sees through the science of his fingers by governing his movements. These things are sufficient to show what the body and tongue are. He is a "knower" through a form equal to his figure and those things which you take from our affairs. He will work for those in need through his own self. Similarly, having been discovered by others, they might draw out their genius for subtle masteries and know how to find subtleties; he would find great things and know the highest forms. He is separated from all other sensible animals; he perceives the good composition of himself and the immensity

<column-break/>

of his own thoughts and wisdom, and the planting of his own qualities. Since man is the understanding treasurer of the world’s creator or his supreme prophet, we exist with the earth and his face within the **greater world**; it is also said that he comprehends the understanding and grasp of the Highest. Man, knowing the world through the senses, does not comprehend everything as if seeing all at once. Yet he sees much, and there are likenesses of man sometimes in plants, and he makes similar forms to them with his own hands <note>A reference to art, sculpture, or perhaps the cultivation of nature.</note>. His qualities are multiplied and explained through nature and works. No other creature has the power of understanding [like him], for they cannot transform themselves or be taught to assimilate to other things. For example, a rooster cannot transform its song, nor a lion the sound of its voice. But man, in his natural voice, has the power to make the voices of others, the sounds of animals, and to change forms and the likeness of things. It is said that at once he can manifest himself in sounds and words, while other animals are in such a disposition as you see. He has a responsive subtlety because he has one part that is "gross" <note>meaning dense or physical</note> and another that is subtle. The subtle part is spoken of in relation to gross motions; in the middle of it, it is soft, and another middle is made; one middle is figured and the other is not. And his mode is not through these two alone; here it is held with a part, and another is absent; there are two, and the other is not mentioned unless the sense is set down in order through another expressed thing. They are in motion by increasing the work. He is composed of dense and subtle matter: he has within himself the subtlety of the grosser earth, and of the air, and the subtlety of fire, and the humidity of water. From these, equality is produced in the motions of the **vital power** <note>original: "virtutis vitalis"; the life force.</note>. Heat rests in the fire, which is in the "axis" by the warmth within it, and the coldness of the water, and the coldness of the power within it from which such elements are constituted, from which every form is composed. He seizes the sign for the useful form in its roundness.

<margin>All the subtler elements, when they reach this place, are generated toward one another; from this it follows that all things reach a unity with each other, just as there is motion in these generated things, and the sense itself proceeds, and it is the matter of motion.</margin>

It is by motion that the sense proceeds, and it appears that the sense appears because the soul remembers it; then the soul is the matter of motion, and it appears that it is higher.

He who desires to know this composite must likewise be good, directed toward goodness; he should be as nothing, at will, assigned to all ranks and removed from all [distracting] thoughts. <margin>Universally</margin>
To speak **universally** <note>original: "Catholice"; likely used here in the sense of "universally" or "generally" rather than strictly "Roman Catholic."</note>, as certain others have professed in their books who speak of a reception and depth occurring within themselves: the will and the depth of reasons is the subtlety of **wisdom** <note>original: "sapientiae"</note> concerning their own men. From the way of nature, they cannot [succeed] without a great multitude [of reasons], and in the matter that is seen, until the received multitude is proved by them. And the thoughts in the said intellects of men are concerning the sanctified man, and to our own [intellect] the completion and perfection is offered, to reach all that is seen, and to serve Him as He willed. In the manifest [sense] then, regarding these sayings and how much the **divine light** <note>original: "lumen divinum"</note> has overflowed, he is able to reach by power and form to the arriving and disposing of the hidden divine things of the aforesaid; because from this we are able [to see] that a certain will shows those things which are in the intellectual realm; and above are the intellects, and he understands all things through all senses under the orders.

# Chapter Seven: In which certain things that are of this world
## are treated, and concerning many other deep properties,
### which we describe in this our book.

**A**nd you should know that all things of this world are ordered without [outward] disorder, just as is subjoined: the Lord of all is the Good of this world, the most noble, high, and most complete. The summit of this world is **God** Himself, who is the factor and creator of all things. And afterward, they follow in the order of sense, just as are the divine worlds. After sense, there are the sensitive perceptions, and these are things that are immovable and others that are movable and changeable from place to place. After this is the order of nature, which is called the **First Mover** <note>original: "primum mobile"; in medieval cosmology, the outermost sphere that moves all others.</note> of the world. And that which is the principle of generation and corruption seen in the world, from here is the wheel of the **fixed stars** even to the limit, just as the other heavens are orders down to the **orb of the moon**. After which is mixed the common nature, the **spirit** <note>original: "spiritus"</note> in which is the order of all the world; hence those things which are in that matter, but it is not [purely so]. After this said matter are the **elements** which operate in this said matter, because the elements do not have operations nor works [directly] in the matter, but subsequently in the order. After these elements follow the **planets**, that is, another subsistence, either deleted or spiritual. And in this order is found an immensity from other orders, by which other orders are balanced in subtlety, which is more noble and higher than all things. And thus descending, they proceed to the rest until you come to active things. And after that, proceeding from the swift even to the noble, until it reaches the summit which is more noble than all things existing beneath the sun and moon. For in it is contained **Fortune** <note>original: "fortuna"; referring to the mutable state of the sublunary world governed by chance and change.</note> according to good things and manifest rest. Wherefore you ought to know that he who labors in Fortune must intend toward these four terms above. And he who labors in this will always have greater fortune and will escape from those things which taste of the contrary. Likewise, know that in men it is similar to what appears in the superior world; those not having fortune [do not have it] because they do not reach for continuity but have labored in vanity; then fortune seems to be changed, but this is only in name. And know that the immense things in this world have other orders and other divisions, which by describing here, lead to all intellects and a more arriving sense. And afterward, he notes in this that there are perfect spirits of the intellects.

<meta>This page transitions from a theoretical discussion of the soul’s perfection to a systematic outline of the cosmic hierarchy. The order is as follows: first is prime matter <note>original: "prima materia"; the basic, formless substance of the universe</note>; after that is high matter; then the elements; then the mixture; then the soul; then nature; then the body; then growth; after that, the animal; then man. Then the merits of man are led and brought forth. But first, it must be understood what high matter is: it is said to be the matter in the celestial realms, just as the matter within the body is called matter itself. Matter is called "common" only because it is nearly the same temperament as the elements; yet, it is not the temperaments in the elements that are the matter, but rather the matter itself, because both the simple body and the mixed body are retentive <note>meaning they can hold or maintain form</note>. Matter is the adaptation of the elements in order to receive form; matter is also the common form because it is simple before receiving forms, and when it receives form, it becomes both matter and form.

Let an example be: just as something is the matter of wood, wood is the matter of its own stool; and when movement and the capacity for movement are mentioned—which is called "mixture"—this now becomes nature. When nature completes the imaginative faculty, and when growth and diminution are completed elsewhere, it then becomes the soul; and it is called a "body" according to its growth and diminution. Growth is spoken of in the animal, but not the soul. And the soul is spoken of in man, but not [simply] man. And man is spoken of in male and female. And the male is formed such that individuals are not unique <note>likely referring to the species-level characteristics over individual ones</note>.

Matter is a co-helper to the creator, ordained to receive form. Matter is divided into two parts: one is simple matter, which receives nothing but the form of the elements, such as earth, water, air, and fire. The other part is common matter, for it is general matter disposed to receive all forms composed of simple qualities, such as heat, cold, dryness, and moisture; and these qualities only exist within these two [types of matter]. All the wise ones note that because matter is disposed to receive all forms, it is left as it is, and is not called anything else by nature except "the body," which is decorated and filled by everything within itself. In these arguments, we say only what is necessary to understand the intention of the senses, because the aforementioned words and logical statements are only imaginations; they are the words that Adam learned from God through his senses so that we might understand. These are the wisdoms of those who faithfully labored in understanding, just as there are truths regarding the stars and their effects. Let this understanding be placed in the intellect, because as we proceed in this book to speak of these gifts together, it will enhance your understanding.

# Chapter Three: On the Workings of the Planets, the Sun, and the Moon

Indeed, certain wise men speaking on the aforementioned matters said that the effect of the **Sun** and its power in this world exists only for the increase and decrease of heat. They said this because they did not understand these <unclear>miraculous</unclear> <unclear>relationships</unclear>; but you should know that if these men had possessed the gate of the planets' power, which is <unclear>declared</unclear> through the <unclear>apparent</unclear> <unclear>assistance</unclear> of the world, they would have seen more. Regarding these effects of the Sun, they said that by the Sun's motions, the six <term>stations</term> <note>The points where a planet appears to stand still before changing direction (retrograde or direct motion).</note> of the planets are proven <unclear>at once</unclear>, and all qualities of those being born are proven.

And they said that the **Moon** has qualities from which she can reveal all her qualities and effects to those who understand. And the <unclear>entirety</unclear> of <unclear>these</unclear> qualities is determined by her distance from the Sun. But after she is separated from the Sun until the first <term>quadrature</term> <note>The "First Quarter" phase, when the Moon is 90 degrees from the Sun.</note>, then there is a greenness <note>original: "uiror"; referring to youthful vitality or the budding of plants.</note> in increasing the moisture of heat, but she is more powerful in moisture than in heat. And then her effect appears in the <unclear>dew</unclear> of the trees and plants, and her effect has a greater increase in herbs and all things dwelling together, and in the trees that rise from the earth.

The second phase is from the end of the first quadrature until the <term>opposition</term> <note>The "Full Moon," when the Moon is 180 degrees from the Sun.</note>. And then her effect appears more clearly in increasing moisture and strength in vegetables and in animals. 

And when she goes from opposition until the second quadrature <note>The "Last Quarter" phase.</note>, then her vigor is in increasing moisture and heat, but it is a greater increase of strength than of moisture. And then her effect appears less in heat than in moisture, and her effect appears in the increasing of the bodies of animals and vegetables; and they have clarified those things which we know well are in all things. And then she works more in strength than in moisture.

And from that second quadrature until the <term>conjunction</term> <note>The "New Moon," when the Moon and Sun are at the same degree.</note>, her motion and works appear to be greatly diminishing in strength—indeed, less than all the other three aforementioned states—although he who reads of these conjunctions which are in <unclear>modern</unclear> <unclear>identities</unclear>...

### Chapter Four: On the movement of the 8th sphere and the fixed stars

**A**ncient sages, who were most learned in the sciences, saw that although the heavens appear to move from East to West (as was previously stated), they later saw and mentally grasped the truth concerning these degrees and the entire motion of the 8th sphere <note>In medieval cosmology, the 8th sphere is the firmament containing the fixed stars, located beyond the seven planetary spheres.</note>. Through many observations, astronomical tables were published by which this motion [...] was made known. Some developed these motions without much usefulness, while others found and made tables that showed progress in these matters, though they were not always consulted.

<margin>In the tables</margin>

In these tables, the motion of the sphere is found at will, and these must by no means be forgotten. It is said that one can know more from the history of the ancients regarding this fixed motion, for it is so great that it is preserved as a lordly instrument of knowledge. This motion completes a cycle every 600 years <note>original: "anni's 6c"; this refers to the theory of "trepidation," a medieval belief that the equinoxes moved back and forth in a 600-year cycle.</note>. It has been given by astronomers as much as is needed to observe the movement in this science. The motion of the 8th sphere belongs to our poles and moves from East to West, and it cannot be otherwise unless it is well-arranged in its parts. When this movement goes from West to East, the sign **kz** <note>Likely a notation for a specific degree or a corrupted zodiac sign.</note> ascends, which in this world brings [...] and when it proceeds from the East, it is shown by the sign **abr'e** <note>Possibly a reference to an Arabic astronomical term or a specific star.</note> which has an effect in this world. This movement is that of the sphere of signs and fixed stars. This movement is not uniform, and it is necessary that you understand this motion and distinguish it in all your most difficult works.

### Chapter Five: On the diversity of this labor; that is, how much each person of these nations has among themselves

...with suffumigations <note>The burning of incense or aromatic herbs as part of a ritual.</note>, charms, prayers, and writings. Fortunate are those who introduced these instruments into the work contained therein.

<margin>It appears</margin>

Many subtle inventors and intelligent men have been found in this science of astrology. This science of astrology is reputable and highly regarded. ## Chapter Four: On the movement of the 8th sphere and the fixed stars

Ancient sages, who were more learned in the sciences, held a theory regarding how much the sun is moved; they found that it advances toward the East by 8 degrees, and afterwards they return toward the West from these 8 degrees. They call such a movement the **motion of trepidation** <note>original: "motum trepidationis"; a medieval astronomical theory that the equinoxes oscillate back and forth rather than moving in a continuous circle.</note> of the 8th sphere <note>The sphere of the fixed stars, located beyond the planetary spheres.</note>. Through many later scholars, astronomical tables were published to demonstrate the validity of this motion, and they made many people knowledgeable about it because of certain great benefits of this motion. First, and more importantly: they created certain things that facilitate the state called "motion" in those tables, and they gave a name to each one according to its constellation <margin>constellation</margin> by which this motion of the sphere might be found at will.

And this is handed down to oblivion in many ways, because it is more important to know about the motion itself than what is manifested from the movement of the figures, where it is announced what it is. One by one, they created these [tables], which indeed change according to the completion of the quadrants every [...] years. In as many, namely [...]. And it has already been told to you through demonstration how much of this motion ought to be visible. In these things, the science is shown to be greater or lesser where the magnitude is changed; it is the motion of the poles of the ecliptic <note>original: "poli ecclia'"; referring to the ecliptic, the sun's apparent path.</note> of the signs, which is a movement from East to West. And trepidations cannot be otherwise except according to these two members. And when the motion is moved from East to West, it shows and signifies what things shall be near in this world. And when it flows from the West to the East, it shows through other signs what effects shall be in this world. And this motion is the specific motion of the signs and the fixed stars, which indeed is not a uniform motion. And it is necessary because of this subtle motion that you [work] through all your works toward the wisdoms of the binding <note>A reference to "binding" or "ligatures," a common term in medieval magic for constraining spiritual forces.</note>.

## Chapter Five: On the various luminous bodies and what kinds each nation has among themselves

I tell you, therefore, that in the judgments from the higher things of the ancients, you will find something very great for this science; afterwards, it is for these [differences] between leaders and those who lead this science. There are many diversities here, for it is known more from science: namely, those who study more in operations. In this, there are those who are named **Agalibya** <note>Likely a corruption of an Arabic term like "Al-Ghaybiya" (pertaining to the unseen/hidden), referring to practitioners of hidden arts.</note>, who act according to the grasp of others. All of this is the science of the stars because of [...]

...by **suffumigations** <note>The ritual burning of incense or herbs to attract or repel spirits.</note> of this kind, and by prayers and writings. They seem to have this science because the science of theology [...] hadres <note>unclear: possibly a corrupted name or technical term</note> of the whole science. By reputation, he is seen to know more, and he operates with suffumigations to bring back a proper, appropriate habit. For these things, there are reasons; they come to the spirit, those of the devil, or names of this kind of the gods of those things to be restored. And for this reason, they do not diminish this science at all. And some [act] erroneously or in vain because they have operated mostly in these manners.

And whatever is proclaimed in the lands of the members, they had the knowledge of the **Indians** <note>Medieval texts often attributed advanced magical and astronomical knowledge to India.</note> and the Essenes(?) equally. And similarly, they have those teachings by which, in whatever way he wishes, he is badly deceived by demons. This is always by the power of God.

And all these subtleties, just as the power of the universe <margin>the power of the universes in turn</margin> adopts them, so they operate in similar ways of moving. Truly changing those reasons, they bring them forth without the power of craftiness, through the motions and works of the modes. And whatever they do from there is a kind of drinkable thing, which is without reason, presented as the reason of the state of the deity, or of nothing, unless they were moved in a maximum way according to the virtues. 

And in all these predicted things are the powers of the virtues of voices; but for others, what was predicted here is of a gross nature, while for others it is found to be led by labor. And they might have the manner of a person in acts of ignorance or passions, according to the world. Indeed, from where he says and they are able to assert (good), which is higher and equivalent toward the world, because of the planting. Which the devil has brought according to the subtlety which they do not perceive, according to the findings with which I shall not believe. And these planets are celestial bodies which are the leaders, each has its own patrons and circles of branches. And according to the higher unity, in all the honor of the celestial ones, by the motion and the prayers in this world, they are seen in the heat of the stars.

<margin>Even though two things are required for understanding, if the body has been purged of **bad humors** <note>original: "malis humoribus"; in medieval medicine, the four humors (blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile) had to be balanced for health and clarity of mind.</note> and is well-ordered in its senses and few temperaments, it seems to be truthful and true; if it is the opposite, because of the spirit, it seems false. They truly believe that another memory appears, at least in a man of poor condition; I find among them a similarity. If the nature of his power is strong, it can overcome impediments. This strength of nature, which is powerful and noble, acts as a natural remedy. They have assigned names to everything that is natural in the body. In sleep, one will see things similar to whatever is most abundant within him. Just as if his body were a sanctuary prepared for him, it appears according to what is depleted. For example, if it were a woman, she acts according to her nature, wanting to discharge the depletion of her matter. If the body is moist with depleted humors, then in sleep he will see **waters**. If it is filled with **melancholy** <note>original: "melancolia"; the humor of black bile, associated with earth, darkness, and depression.</note>, he will see monstrous and horrible things in his dreams. If the matter is "black" <note>likely referring to "atra bilis" or black bile</note>, he will see smoke, a black dog, and similar things appearing in his dreams. 

Omens are made known in this way, and there is a freedom by which we speak of the dreamer's dreams: those which are true are perceived through omens. If all the powers that are formed are strong and pure for receiving information, then that which is wise in the spirit seems to be moved, and it leads itself into the things it sees. Through this, we can attain the power of the future and the understanding of things that exist. All of this lies in its strength. In the same way that the lower powers of intention are formed, they appear separated from the senses; they leave the senses behind and operate in the medium between the sense and the soul—namely, in the spirit. 

When these two are found, they must be understood according to the rule: if the body is purged of bad humors and ordered in its senses and temperaments, the vision appears truthful and true. If the reverse is true because of the spirit, it appears false. Thus, the intellective power holds dominance. When these powers align, it is what we call prophecy. It is one of the two powers by which signs are formed; they are complete and clean from all impurities. The soul then appears separate from the spirit, and the intention is made clear. Because of this, the dominant power can reach things distant from the spirit—things the soul reaches through the senses. 

This happens in those called "complete" in their sensory comprehension. But only the wise man precedes others in sustaining these powers. If these two powers are smoothed out, they possess **prophetic power** <note>original: "vim propheticam"</note>. This cannot occur except in **starred men** <note>original: "hominibus stellatis"; individuals born under particularly auspicious or powerful astrological alignments.</note> in whom the prophetic faculties are completely poured in according to the divine disposition of God. He then infuses and spreads the prophetic spirit by means of the senses. Such natural prophecies are as they are in themselves, and thus the sense appears in all powers, eventually attaining intellect. Because of these senses, it is said they see into the reality of things.

For they desired this connection, which belongs only to those having **greater fortune** <note>original: "fortunam maiorem"; a term in astrology referring to the most positive planetary influences, usually Jupiter.</note>. It should be known that "greater things" include good morals and desires for the divine; we do not find this among the wicked. 

We know that those who lived by laws and justice were the ones who aided the power of the intellect in truth. This matter and the method of attaining that "greater fortune" involve the harmony of the world's things and their qualities, joined together. This specific property is what we call the "part of science." Now see: it proceeds from the three levels of the sensible until it reaches the other. Let it be sought until they arrive at **metaphysics**, through which completion is given to man. Through these "fortunes" of forms, he is made perfect.

The founder of the Law <note>original: "conditor legis"; likely referring to a religious figure or a philosophical legislator like Plato or Moses.</note> seems to say the same: a life of liberty is not worthy of being remembered unless it is the life of some future world, because the present life, in respect to that one, is to be considered as nothing. 

Now let us return to our purpose. He says they divide science into two parts. We have shown how they speak of bodies and their affairs, which we wish to produce from their effects. This is according to the operations of the **ancient sages**, who made various figures in **images** <note>original: "ymaginibus"; here meaning astrological talismans or statues designed to draw down celestial power.</note> and infused powers into them through their prayers, so that they could perform divine acts. These images are like the elements to a body. Because of this, those who make them call them miracles and likenesses; they have the law of the strong because their works are established upon natural powers. If natural powers were unchangeable, it would be said that just as the **magnet** <note>original: "lapis adimanra" (corruption of *adamans*); the lodestone or diamond, often used as an analogy for invisible attraction.</note> attracts, so too does the spirit within these images.

### Chapter 8: On the virtues of images, the materials from which they may be obtained, how they require the power of celestial bodies, and how the power of the planets operates within them.

You should know that although it is said there is a certain power in nature arising from the property of the planets—acting according to the power of the agent—if it possesses a manifest nature in that work, and especially if it grants such operations from celestial power through the things themselves (rather than just through a manifest nature already within them), then that work will be stronger and more effective. We speak of these works appearing spiritually according to the ruler. And this is just as we know that **choler** <note>original: "colera"; the humor associated with fire, heat, and dryness.</note> has its own power. This is because of the commonality it shares with others in heat and dryness, to which its nature is seen to be assimilated. It is also evident in sulfurous garments: when they perform any action by the power and likeness already existing within them, then that operation is manifested in the **decan** <note>original: "dicano"; a ten-degree division of the zodiac used in astrology to refine the influence of a planet.</note> and appears more clearly. In this way do talismans operate, for a talisman is nothing other than the power found remaining in lower bodies. Because that matter finds nothing to produce by itself, it receives the influence of those celestial bodies or planets to achieve this perfection. Once found, the planets create a likeness from themselves to flow into the material bodies of the talismans; then the talisman will be strong in itself for all the effects we seek and work through it. And the likeness with the planets makes the work more complete. For example, if you wish to arrange a visible likeness in the form through which the maker wants the talisman to act, he must choose the matter in which it is to be made and ordered; and know that all things produced in likeness to one another

<column-break/>

agree in their similarities regarding the powers from the influence of the planets. Those who gave the **canon** <note>original: "canonem"; the rule or authoritative standard of the art.</note> thus ordained that a valid and complete image, with its own proper effects, is created when the components are joined in that talisman; the effect will then appear and the work of that planet will be manifested. Just as it happens with writing—when the hands are able to perform it, the writing is manifested and appears to men—so it is with images produced from figures at the proper time. Therefore, we ought not to depart from the positions of the trees or anything done in the workings of stones, until the **Shepherd** <note>original: "pastor"; likely a reference to Hermes Trismegistus, often called the "Shepherd of Men" or a legendary source of hermetic wisdom.</note> wrote the compositions of them and the parts that are in his hands, and instructed them how to shape them so that they might never fail in those works. And the stars increase many of these effects; but if the alignment departs, that which was in the proper disposition perishes. We see this in the **ant** and the **harvestman** <note>original: "formica et opiliones"; "opiliones" can mean shepherds, but here refers to daddy-long-legs or similar creatures, used as examples of natural instinct.</note>, which, though they are animals, can do things by their own industry that men do, yet they are preserved without fail through the observation of the hours and many such things. These correspond to the compositions and agree with the workings and dispositions of nature and the powers of the planets. Similar works occur through the voice in known and suitable members; just as the disposition of bodies formed in matter responds to the one who observes it, until it reaches the disposition suitable for the effect of that power. Hence, nature performs its work from the planets through their own powers until that work properly reaches its effect. This is the way of the worlds and the waters from which stones are produced: first, there is clear water, and afterward it comes upon the earth, washing over it until it is placed in a likeness of **vegetable milk** <note>original: "vegetabili lacte"; likely a reference to a sap-like or calcifying fluid in the process of petrification.</note>; then, through nature moving it, it is finally nourished by rule and assimilated into stone. It change its own form and figure completely and unchangeably. In this manner, matter knows how to receive form, and it is preserved in all things born in this world; in such a way, the matter putrefies until we see the disposition that afterward becomes that tree, which through a certain influence takes a form and figure suitable to the completion of its shape.

The **form of Mercury** according to the opinion of the sage Mercury is the form of a man with the head of a rooster and the sign of calculation; he has feet like the feet of an eagle, and in his right and left hands he holds coins <note>original: *denarios*</note>; under his feet are signs called "heridici"; this is his form.

The **form of Mercury** according to the *Picatrix* is the form of a standing man with wings spread on his shoulders; in his right hand he holds a staff for [pigs? suitors?] <note>original: *vallum procorum*; possibly a corruption of a caduceus or a specific agricultural tool</note>, and in his right hand "praise" <note>original: *laudem*; likely laurel or a spear as noted above</note>, and in his left a round wheel; he appears in whatever manner he wishes; and this is his form.

The **form of the Moon** according to Mercury is the form of a woman with a beautiful face before a dragon in a chariot; she has flying wings on her head, but one flying above her head; on each arm are two scrolls <note>original: *volumina*</note>; there is one dragon above her head and another dragon under her feet, and each dragon has two heads as seen below; this is her form.

### Chapter 2: Regarding the Signs of the Faces of Old Age and Their Effects

The ancient wise men <note>original: *sapientes antiqui*</note>, who have spoken of these things until now, have proven many most worthy things through many reasons. On account of their authority, we wish to be a little more extensive and diffuse, so that it may finally come from our purpose; and this especially without the reasons which are necessary, and without which we are able to proceed from our purpose through the doctrine which intends to study this science. What one studies in it without profit, yet with utility to this whole world and to the world similar to man—for we know the wise men possessed many things, yet we do not attain that except with great difficulty of study and labor. We attain that which we wish outside of ourselves, away from the human anxieties that torment us so much. First <unclear>speaking</unclear> of it, they strove most to study it with good introductions and memories, which they possessed through the good towards this Intellect; through memory, it is strengthened. Again, we understand how to know deeply, and as much as we are able, one possesses a memory with an extended sense of preservation. In these things, not all are equal, where diversities of science are seen on account of their good memory and intellect. We <unclear>find</unclear> this, and therefore the wise men said that where he himself is and the whole is, it is said that Intellect is given to all. Finally, they are seen with all the clarity of their science, so that they might be rational in power, and might act through the dispositions of their writer. A word in which the first does not follow, just as an animal is the same: to understand brings forth the act, and it is strong in that against a weak work, and by simple deeds it is weak. Just as we see such a thing to be, that a strong field is suited for slowness with great labor, and it is said against the activation of slowness in things that do not have the same good Intellect; for good memory and Intellect are nurtured excessively.

## On the face of Aquarius

The **first face of Aquarius** belongs to Saturn, in which one may create images <note>original: *ymagines*; these are astrological talismans or amulets</note> for the sake of love and friendship, and for protecting companions, as well as for bonds, pledges, vengeance, and for seizing and guarding captives; in these, one creates images on clean materials, etc., both for vengeance and for reconciling a multitude with one another, and so forth.

## On the face of Pisces

The **first face of Pisces** belongs to Jupiter, in which one creates an image for fishing in the sea and in good streams, and a voice <note>perhaps a "word of power" or invocation</note> for possessing all things... and in the water of great rivers. It is also for strengthening friendship and for calling forth rivers in times of necessity, and for catching the strongest fish with a line and various instruments. Their image is a ship, and in whichever face it may be, the image is for obtaining love, friendship among a multitude, and the delight of the soul and of beasts; otherwise, it is the face of one responding to every hour.

# Here begin the images of Hermes Trismegistus for all infirmities of the limbs

Hermes Trismegistus says in his *Book of Images* regarding health that one can imagine every single property useful to the members of the human body. Let the sign be made upon very dense <note>original: *uiscosas*; likely meaning hard or fine-grained stones suitable for carving</note> stones for the sake of love, so that a seal is made in which you shall carve the **form of a lion**. This should be done while the Sun is in Leo, in the first or second face, and in the corner of the East or South. The Moon must not be in its fall <note>original: *sub domo*; referring to a position of astrological weakness</note>, and let the two aspects <note>likely referring to the Sun and Moon</note> not look upon Saturn nor Mars, nor be receding. Within twenty-four hours, this is taken for the loins and the belly. It is necessary that whenever the image is made, it is for those who have suffered greatly. Furthermore, some things are sealed with that seal and they pass away; truly, I shall give that which has been sealed in a drink <note>This describes a common medical-magical practice where a seal's impression was "washed" into a liquid for the patient to consume</note> and the person will be immediately liberated. For I have been experienced not only in [curing] blood through this first decan, but in visions and desires. I know this regarding the suffering of the limbs according to the manner of the forms in the equations of the planets.

Another figure, which is from the end of the image and its properties, is for all infirmities of the **head and ears**. These should be made in the hour of the Sun, in the first or second hour. This figure is more powerful if it be springtime, during the waxing of the Moon or Sun. Let this figure be made for health:

<sig>A</sig>

<column-break/>

Let it lead the impulses of the belly in Aquarius. Let the name <note>likely the name of the patient or a specific planetary name</note> not be in Scorpio, which is the house of depression <note>the sign where the planet's influence is at its lowest</note>. Let us turn ourselves toward the Moon, and if this figure be from the first degree of Aries up to the fifth, it first causes it to be in the second face. Then, as one of the ancients says, he who makes a similar drink at any hour for the living ought to look well upon the square <note>original: *in quadrum*; an astrological aspect of 90 degrees</note>. If it be the Sun or Jupiter, let the whole operation be done in the hour of the Sun, as it is told by the Moon, and it is said that in the day and the hour of the Sun, it should be made in either tin, silver, or red copper, which is sometimes said to be carried by wives.

# And the figure of Taurus against the infirmity of gout

The **form of Taurus** is one placed for the head and all its infirmities. <note>The text here conflates the head and gout, which in medieval medicine were sometimes linked through the theory of "descending humors" or "catarrhs" falling from the head to the joints.</note> Let it be made in the first face, from the first degree through the fifteenth up to the twentieth. Let Saturn not be in Pisces, nor the Moon in Scorpio. If the hands fail, it is also necessary to change [the timing]. One waits for the day and hour of the Sun, or if it be done under the lunar hour, let it be in the second face. Accordingly, when someone fears a facial affliction, let it be placed over the infirmity of the bile and over the infirmity of the belly. Let the form be made in the second hour; let it be large, with a small face but large eyes, and let it be made in the city.

# Against infirmities of the spleen

The **form of Gemini** <note>original: *Gennii*; a corruption of *Gemini*</note> is one placed for the spleen in the body and all its infirmities. Let it be made from the first degree up to the tenth. If the Sun is over it, it is true; but if Jupiter were in Gemini, it would be more powerful, since the Gemini rule the spleen. The Gemini rule the bodies while holding... to the servant in every man up to the navel, and from the navel to the forehead, which in every body is in the house of Mars. It should be made during the waxing [Moon] by day and in the hour of the Sun, in the first face, on the first day and in the hour of Jupiter for other members.

# Against every infirmity of the belly

The **form of Cancer** is one placed over all infirmities of the belly. Let it be made in the first face from the first degree up to the fifth. In the second face, it immediately addresses the infirmity; it is said to be composed for all infirmities of the **intestines**. Let neither Saturn nor Jupiter be retrograde in Mars, nor in Taurus, and let there be an increase of the Moon or let the Sun be in the [appropriate sign] after midday.
