### Of the Head of the Dragon
<note>The "Head of the Dragon" (Caput Draconis) refers to the North Node of the Moon, while the "Tail" (Cauda Draconis) refers to the South Node. In medieval astrology, these were treated as "shadow planets" with powerful reinforcing or diminishing effects.</note>

**And you should know** that the nature of the Head of the Dragon is one of increasing; whatever it is with, if it be with fortunate planets <note>The "benefics," usually Jupiter and Venus</note>, it will increase their goodness and strength, and if it be with unfortunate planets <note>The "malefics," usually Saturn and Mars</note>, it will increase their harm and misfortune. Similarly, the Tail of the Dragon is of a diminishing nature; if it be with fortunate planets, it lessens their goodness, unless it be that its own evil and diminution are [neutralized]; and soon we shall treat these aforesaid things with subtle diligence.

### Chapter 2: On the properties of the signs existing in the three aforesaid parts, namely plants, animals, and minerals

**And each** of the planets has its own property in things, just as each of the signs has its own property in things. And first, the **Sun** with Leo <note>The Sun is the planetary ruler of the sign Leo</note> governs among the members of the body the right eye, the pupil of the eye, and the nerves; and of colors, saffron-yellow, red, and black; and of flavors, the bitter; and of locations, high and very high places, and places in which broad spaces are radiant; and of metals, gold; and of all those things which are worked by fire; and of leading animals, those having covered feet <note>original: "pedes cooperiuntur," likely referring to hoofed animals (ungulates)</note>.

**Taurus** governs among the members of the body the neck, the arteries, and the belly; and of [growing] things, all the plants of the seasons, gardens, and pleasant places; and of trees, all tall trees and those bearing clean fruit, and those which do not have fruit [but grow near] water; and all good odors; and those having [sweet] flavors; and of animals, all four-footed animals and those having hooves.

## Of Sagittarius

Sagittarius governs the buttocks and legs in the human body, as well as the fine marks on the body and those that are most prominent. Its colors are rose-like, such as reddish-pinks, deep reds, all pale reds, and saffron <term>saffron: a golden-yellow or orange-yellow color derived from the crocus flower</term>. Its flavors are bitter. It is associated with the orbs around a king and with fire. Among stones, it claims emeralds and red pearls. Its animals include humans, birds, and horned beasts.

## Of Capricorn

Capricorn governs the knees of the body and the parts below the knees, such as the shins. It is associated with reds, reddish-purple, and all colors leaning toward red and black. Its flavors are somewhat harsh and the taste of swampy mud. It is linked to a single king and to brazilwood <note>original: "brasilias"; a source of red dye in the Middle Ages</note>, things found in water, and horn-colored red. It governs four <unclear>of which</unclear> and the countryside where we see reptiles and mice, and places that are dark yet fortunate. Its flavors are all bitter, as some say of the walnut, and it governs all female labors and a certain portion of water beasts—specifically those in snaky places—and serpents.

## Of Aquarius

Aquarius governs the ankles and heels of the body, along with the legs. Its colors are saffron, lead-gray, and red. Its flavors are sweet. It is associated with the mud of the waters and with death in places where we see red stones, and similar things like long <unclear>watery</unclear> objects, and thus under <unclear>the first part</unclear> in the figure <unclear>of the nut(?)</unclear> <unclear>just as</unclear> it possesses.

## Of the Sign of Pisces

Pisces governs the feet, toes, and nails. Its colors are green, leaning toward black, and well-saturated colors. Its flavors are sweet. Its locations are places of moisture, formerly in watery places. Among stones, it governs red ones, as well as white stones, crystals, pearls, and everything born in the water. Among animals, we see aquatic creatures and red ones; these are their properties.

## Chapter 7: On the figures and colors of garments, the planetary fumigations, and the colors of the faces of the signs

Now we shall speak of the colors <term>tinctures: the specific colors or dyes associated with celestial bodies</term> of the planets. The color of Saturn is like burnt wool, as it appears. That of Mars is red. The Sun's is a golden, purplish red. Venus's is red in the manner of honey and milk <note>Likely a creamy pink or pale coral color</note>. Mercury's is green. The Moon's is a reddish-white.

## Here begin the forms of the planets according to the custom in the book sent to King Alexander, which is called the Book of the Seven Planets. These descriptions are highly necessary in this science.

The form of Saturn is that of a gloomy black man, wrapped in cloth, having the head of a hyena and holding a sickle in one hand.
The form of Jupiter is that of a man wearing the garments of a Jew <note>In medieval art, this typically indicated a scholar, judge, or a figure of the "Old Law," often wearing a specific hat or draped robe</note>, sitting upon a throne; and this is his form.
The form of Mars is that of a man riding upon a lion, brandishing a spear in one hand; and this is his form.
The form of Mercury is that of a naked man writing, riding upon a horse; and this is his own form.
The form of the Sun is that of a man whose face is said to be beautiful, having a crown on his head; in his right hand he holds a scepter, and in his left a small knife, with a dragon beneath his feet <note>original: "diversum draconem"</note> having similar hands and feet.
The form of Venus is that of a beautiful youth <note>The Latin "invenis" is likely "iuvenis," which could be a young man or woman, though usually depicted as female in this context</note> holding a comb in one hand and a feather or pen in the other, with hair spread out; this is her form.
The form of the Moon is that of a man riding upon a hare; and this is his form.

# The Saying of Aristotle

It must also be known that this image is called an image because the dominions of its spirits are joined. And it should also be known that the motion mentioned in these books regarding them refers to the spirits of their spirits, just as they are in the world—like a spirit that activates its body without disturbance, healthy and unharmed. These are works crafted by hands. They exist in the nature of the will and the works of the spirit, devising through their thought and the "plectrum" <note>original: *plectrum*; used here metaphorically as a tool or instrument of the mind</note> which is said to be drawn from the composite world (or from composite things) by the Indian [philosopher] at the appropriate time in which one composes. He intends just as the lord of the spirit gives elevated light to names, like solar rays; thus the spirit gives light to have superintendence without [physical] light, and it reaches the shadowy light, and the rays of their power are diffused, and the thing is illuminated. Because of this, something is announced through the light of the sun. This is how they operate: spirits are everywhere, and when they regard worldly things in their own way, they cause motion, and through that motion, they are attracted to its world. And so they are infused into the matter itself according to how it holds the fourfold <note>the four elements or qualities</note>, and these are the namings.

<margin>And if you should need some petition while you are in his petition, for then he who is the duty [or guilt]... that sentence which Complete Nature... they are applied to answer Complete Nature... immediately Complete Nature.</margin>

## The Saying of the Wise Hermes
Hermes said that "Complete Nature" <term>natura completa: in medieval hermeticism, this refers to a magician's "Perfect Nature" or personal tutelary spirit that acts as a bridge to the divine</term> belongs only to the wise, whose roots are named and in which the wisdom of Hermes is refined. Someone bound me by the depth of this "Complete." And Hermes said to those questioning him what it is said to be; and through this, his Complete Nature would be for those questioning him... they are immediately those who are the duty, which sentence is applied to Complete Nature to answer "Complete Nature." Afterward, they are through the spirit with the planet governing it in the nature of things. And if it is said how appropriately the terms and rules of the world’s intelligence are closed, it is because they can hardly be understood, since the world is opposite. He foresaw that they are from the highest, for the world is the world. Unite with the aforementioned because "Complete Nature," or the spirit, has its own wisdom... Let those who look upon it see it pronounced in the mixture, and the spirit is freed from the world to its effect; it provides and rejoices because it is not of the perfected spirits. In knowledge and similar things, and thus operated by its own nature, it is seen by its own virtue; and its influence is restricted, according to the philosophers, by its natural spirit. You should understand the inclinations through the sayings of the world; it is necessary for the wise man to be honored, for it would be impossible to say anything to it unless one is similar to the natural spirits found—so erroneously described—that they demonstrate by the disposition of the planets in their own domain.

## A certain wise man and the works of the greatest of the wise among the Recipients

One who wishes to know the power of the operation of the planets—as it is said in the book of the ancients concerning the works of magic—ought to know the will of the planets so that he may be able to obtain something from them according to his own will through the immediate line of the Lord. And let him be altogether careful not to rely upon any other ruler. Then, purify your body and your clothes from all filth; let him offer a perfect mind, and with a clean mind, he approaches the planets in his petition. And when he wishes to speak to a planet to which he proposes his petition, let him first bring in the designated things of that planet... from its sustenances and supports... these are prayers in which all things are summarized. And they are to be pronounced in the following ways, and let him know in his petitions how to submit to the warnings of the operation, saying what is desired; then let him know well and briefly the appropriate petitions of each of the planets.

### Since all things that we have in our petitions must be asked for

Common things are asked for in a noble and clean way, such as in the riches of generated honors, in labors that return pure results, such as in inheritances, and for men by the grace of prayers for their kindred and all their entrances. And so in the government of lords, it is said according to the position or change [of the planets], and it amends misfortune. Furthermore, in all things, petitions are found for each of the aforementioned: those for Saturn and those things which are assigned to his nature, and you should ask those of him as is said later. And if anyone [asks] in our petition, Jupiter will help. And he will give the very thing petitioned, for he is more powerful than other planets in some of our petitions, as they are divided by his attributes.

#### To ask of Jupiter those things which consist in lordships, such as:

Petitions of sublime lords, powers, prelates, the wise, the prudent, laws, judges, good men, and the benefit of philosophers, kings, monks, clerics, soldiers, confessors; petitions of peace and of great meditations, and of everything that is similar to these reasons, one should ask of them.

#### To ask of Mars those things which consist in his nature, such as:

Petitions against soldiers, officials, attackers, and spirited acts...

He is loved and, while he refuses, he turns away those who abhor good things. He is remembered for his words and for administering many good things to those who work, while detesting evil men.

## On the qualities of Mars

Mars is powerful and strong. In form, he is a condemner and the author of evils; he signifies punishments, evil works, and the depopulating and wasting of houses out of <unclear>nudity</unclear> <note>original: "nutate"; possibly a scribal error for "nuditate" (destitution)</note>. He is the prohibitor of many things, the bringer of fires, smoke, blood, and the movement of violent impulses. In his influence, there are evil signs and indirect oppressions, sorrows of the human mind, and the destruction of goods, the ruin of cities, battles, and the armies of men. He brings discords, anxieties, wretched punishments, doubts, terrors, and produces headlong flight, dances, and foolishness. He produces all things that are possessed in the manner of his cursed state. He is the joy of the physician and the worldly sorrow of the <unclear>medraru</unclear> <note>possibly "medullarum" (the marrow/inner depths)</note>, and he pledges the vanity of gifts. Throughout his whole life, he is the destroyer of the sun's peace, ruining cities, lands, and those speaking in forbidden laws in the manner of the <unclear>medrarum</unclear> legalities. He desires pledges of favor, falsehoods, and the evil seeds of human works. In the world, he forbids women, just as when beasts and other animals are carried away; and he condemns many on account of other enemies, sons, and <term>vocativas</term> <note>likely "vocations" or "callings," though here in a negative or condemned sense</note>, even in their just affairs.
<margin>and evil thoughts</margin>
He holds thoughts of the mind such as plunder, and in labors and ruins, he signifies the robbery of roads and the "breaking" of travelers at night, the movement of gates, and the evil-doing of those who cleanse the world of things; and all these turn away from lawful gains.

## On the quality of the Sun

The Sun is powerful and strong, both for good and for evil. In clean proportion, he acts just as he condemns; he brings both good and bad fortune, sense and intellect, the exaltation of high honors, and promises. He reveals himself to free men, as well as to the healthy, the good, those desiring <unclear>rimasos</unclear> <note>perhaps "rimas" (cracks/details) or "remotos" (distant things)</note> in cleanliness and merits.

<column-break/>

He shows things to be done sumptuously. He rejoices in the friendship of God. He brings laws, swiftness, and striving. He condemns those who allege many things against friends in the depths of <unclear>dertuis</unclear>. He acts both well and sometimes poorly; he works good through <term>legality</term> and the meeting of promises for all men. He makes one love the good and a great eloquence, giving eloquent responses in all lawful matters. Regarding divine and worldly things, he increases the highest appetite for fame, the good of men, their bonds, exaltation, and royal honors, granting them all legality and goodness. His property is to make one upright toward other men in the glory of the highest way of living. He animates necessary wars and worldly operations out of a love for ornaments, and he acts most freely toward the crowns of kings and the high-born.

## On the quality of Venus

Venus is cold and moist <note>In medieval astrology, Venus was associated with the "phlegmatic" qualities of water</note>. She signifies cleanliness and <term>purity</term> <note>original: "munditiam"; can mean physical cleanliness, elegance, or moral purity</note> through all games and the music of the <term>barbiton</term> <note>original: "barbiturm"; an ancient lute or lyre-like instrument</note>. She loves singing, joys, and likewise cleverness, laughter, and the jokes of beautiful form. She loves the beating of instruments truly played and the return of the instrument. She loves brides and those who are led astray, and she is present in these good things. Her appetite is to perform every game of judgment and the rare paths of purity through all things. They speak of desire and, as if with a Roman love, they trust in confidence. She loves beautiful appetites; the harsh and the youthful love her, and she renders bearded men with high-mindedness and brings the joy of rare affections. She loves to meditate on legality and to seek good appetites and the will of the world’s royal <term>indices</term> <note>guides or signs</note>. She has envy toward false oaths in the greed for discovery. She greatly despises the father; she eats quite improperly but seeks <unclear>indetimentas</unclear> <note>possibly "indumenta" (garments/clothing)</note> and to enjoy herself in a joined state. She loves <term>vocativas</term> <note>callings or voices</note> and makes boys be well-spoken. She loves the quality of justice in affairs, the cleanliness of ornaments, and being among mirrors and women, and so she is spoken of well by men. In the inspiration of the entry of the <unclear>theri</unclear>, she grants the holiness of rare things, making one eloquent with gemstones. Having a sweeter eloquence, she possesses the desert of the worldly movement—that is, she is the sustainer of men, unless God or a destroyed wall assigns power where she is weak. By her will, she designates the weak in lawsuits and battles, or the unwilling. She signifies the appetite for all composed forms, which she prefers to provide for her own will. She is right to work out of her magnificent deeds, loving the greatest purity, upright callings, the observance of laws, and obedience. She appears desirable to the wise and the philosophers.

<header>On the quality of Mercury</header>

# Mercury is changeable, moving from one nature to another and blending with others, for he takes on the nature of other planets he joins. With the good he is good; with the evil, he is evil. As Ptolemy says in the *Centiloquium* <note>original: "centiloquio"; a famous medieval collection of 100 astrological aphorisms traditionally attributed to the astronomer Claudius Ptolemy</note>, he provides logic, good eloquence, true intelligence, and a deep and profound knowledge of all literature. He grants a good memory, a quickness of grasp, agility, and an aptitude for teaching the sciences. For those laboring in secrets and philosophy, he gives a subtle and good understanding, poetry and meter, geometry, astrology, necromancy, augury, and grammar that is softly agreeable. He easily grasps things regarding the making of medicinal potions. In secret labors, he is diligent; yet he can also produce false inquiries. He publishes good books, yet his face is unchangeable <note>perhaps suggesting a "poker face" or stoicism</note>. He governs the keepers of account books and the writers of the scribes, seeking to please the wise while remaining hidden in his own status. He is a lover of the <term>prosopon</term> <note>original Greek: "prosopon"; meaning a mask, face, or the persona one presents to the world</note>, a lover of cries of humility, mercy, gentleness, sense, and joys. He brings about innovations, wonders, and destruction, impressing mercy and a desire for good servants among men. He finds pleasure in dwelling in seats and habitations, and in his habit of concealing his will when thinking evil thoughts. He can be a lie or he can be worldly; in his falsehood, he composes and ends dissension for the one who fears. In all works, he is swift and unstable; alone, he is unstable and bold in great matters. In all things, he is daring in the manner by which he seeks a great end through subtleties. He sustains the curiosity and care for innovations and acts as a supporter of men and all those held under authority.

->On the quality of the Moon<-

# The Moon is cold and moist. She signifies excellent writers of great science, good sense in thought, an outstanding memory, and the best kind of speech—though sometimes she brings boasting. She is said to be orderly in her movements and necessary in her effects, through which she seeks the fortune of good character to be held toward men. She possesses a great desire for stirring the heart and for the pleasure of many people. She brings forth a ruler over <unclear>evil ones</unclear> and, through men, she is a bringer of good habits, seeking joy in the beauty and decoration of the house. She stands by new sciences, being herself worthy of things such as great astrology and other secrets. She brings marriages to those who present themselves, loves to procreate children, <unclear>commands</unclear> those who love holy honors, and brings good things to their parents.

His zone and any <unclear>acts</unclear> of the terms or <unclear>mixtures</unclear>, whether malignant or truthful, of which all evil is nothing, must be ruled by his table <note>likely a planetary square or mathematical table used in ritual timing</note> in the masculine quarters—namely in their light and above. Then, one shall diligently see where he is in affinity with a planet standing opposite to him in quality. He <unclear>renews</unclear> Saturn from infirmity; and if he is held in such a way as to be truly of good will, he returns <unclear>elevated</unclear> so that, by the law of his abundant will, it is clear he will not deny anything. And when that same planet is in its cause or "root" <note>original: "radice"; the starting point or radical position in a chart</note> from an angle, it is like a man of the earth with <unclear>bad</unclear> will; it is clear that if he acts, requests are not denied. If one wishes to speak more at the <unclear>root</unclear>, in all separate matters, he denies all dissensions that exist within the body. In the manner of <unclear>seizing</unclear> <unclear>unequally</unclear>, he speaks his senses and reasonings; at the same time, let the impression you carry go toward the good work assigned to such things. ### The Opinion of Other Wise Men
There are also other wise men who pray to Jove himself with other incense offerings and prayers. ### The Saying of Cassius in the Book of Metaphysics
<margin>Cassius</margin>
As Cassius says in his book of Metaphysics <note>likely referring to a pseudo-epigraphical source attributed to a "Cassius" or a corruption of a known philosopher’s name</note>, in order to escape the dangerous times at sea by the power of Cassius <note>original: "virtute Casio"; perhaps meaning 'by the power of the shrine of Zeus Cassius'</note>, it is necessary to worship Jove himself in this manner, and you shall say: "God save you, noble planet, high radiant star! Honored indeed; for in you, God is able to provide spirit and sense, a good reputation to the one swearing a firm oath, and clean bodies; you who are in the highest law and judgment, who guides both life and those sailing on the sea, and preserving them in this sea. Therefore, I [call upon] you

for the strength which God has placed in you, so that pure and in accord with his light, you may help me among men, and [so that] you can cleanse me of the filth of the world and the vices of the night; and that from my pious <unclear>senses</unclear> I may be able to understand. And if your work has been duly heard, you will approach the likeness of a sweet lit candle; if you do not see it, know that your work is not done. ### Chapter eight: On the manner of the prayers with which the Nabateans <note>original: "neptini"; a common medieval Latin corruption referring to the Nabateans, the ancient people of the Near East credited with deep agricultural and astrological secrets</note> prayed to the Sun and Saturn, the ways in which they spoke with them, and drew forth their spirits and effects.

The sages of the Nabateans said that petitions [are made] through the operation of heat and that lamps are like simplicity; in a certain way, it is said that it should be understood that the Moon assists the Sun—that is, in terms of his effects—nor do they need her except as they do for the other planets. Similarly, the other planets follow the Sun in their effects and obey him as messengers; therefore, the dispositions of the Sun proceed among the aforementioned beings. All those effects are within him as if he were the prince of all of them. The concord of the following planets assists him in his effects. Similarly, the stars provide help, and men obey him through our humility; they assist from above in his effects, nor is it necessary that he should have his own assistance [from elsewhere]. And these parts of the prayers are to be made to the Sun through him.

### Prayer of the Nabateans to the Sun

> We pray, we honor, and we praise you, most high Lord, God of the Sun. God who rules over all who dominate the world; world most pure, highest, and most happy; with power and governance. You are situated in a high place, possessing a great kingdom, full of light, sense, and intellect, powerful and honorable. You are the source of good for all generations, and through your power, all things are to be governed after governance itself. Through you, all growing things flourish, and through you, all things remain in their strength. You, in your inner effects given to us, provide beauty and honor, and the power to remain in your virtue. We salute you, we praise you, we honor you, and we pray through obedience and humility. We open all our desires to you and ask you for all things necessary for us within your reign. And you [grant] this from the world of governance, which you [hold] by the virtue given and your own direction. To you we dispose our wills through God. May the evils which are emitted from us, whatever they may be, be absent and driven away by your light, which obeys you with help. You live in the virtue of providence from which the effect is given. You are God, hidden in your heaven, and the speeches of the other planets always obey your light, and all things [come] from your own nature...

And may the Lord be praised by us always, through infinite ages of ages. Amen.

### Prayer of the Sages of Chaldean Agriculture

<margin>This is the prayer for the sages of Chaldean Agriculture</margin>
The sages of Chaldean agriculture <note>The "Chaldean Agriculture" refers to a legendary body of knowledge attributed to ancient Mesopotamian magicians</note> said that they prayed to Saturn with this prayer. First, they observed that they themselves were destined [for the task]. In their name there should be a distinction; in their name there should be [an absence] of accidents <note>In philosophy, "accidents" are non-essential properties; here it likely means avoiding unlucky occurrences</note> so that we might be under your studies. Nor should our God be in <term>retrogradation</term> <note>When a planet appears to move backward in the sky, often considered a weakened or ill-omened state in astrology</note>, but by a certain likeness of God, we may be liberated from all impediments through the distribution of the prayer made to him. And a fumigation of dew-moistened items should be burned as described—fourteen were all burned together—along with the pleasant parts of trees. They should place two [items] at the head of his image: first, a golden image upon a stone or upon black <unclear>lead</unclear> <note>original: "rani nigrum"; likely "plumbi nigri," the metal associated with Saturn</note>. And so it will behoove you to be [cautious] of his evil name from above. For from him proceed all evils, losses, and weeping. On the contrary, they [the stars] give to all poverty, enduring pains, foulness, and lamentations. And he produces signs... he is the root of those who are damned. But when he is in a good disposition, in his <term>exaltation</term> <note>The specific sign of the zodiac where a planet's influence is most powerful and positive</note>, he signifies purity, length of life, height, joys, honor, riches, inheritance, and the durability of inheritance among children and grandchildren. For goodness is as truth is from the Sun. And while he is in the middle of the sky and in his strongest [state], he is taught from the middle by his own elevated course in the angle... as the first of the three sages of Chaldean agriculture who made this prayer to Saturn. And the petitions which they wished to ask from him, they prepared immediately... in which they wished to have the dismissal of all words, the tenor of which is such:

> Prayer: We raise ourselves onto our feet; we pray and honor you through obedience and humility. The doctrine of God in the present is from those spirits; they are all the power reaching toward this world concerning the climates and generations; they descend from the aforesaid, by which prayers and wonders and effects may be made for those invoking them. From them is denoted both poverty and those things flowing out, for they themselves send down divine friends. They have bodies with which they are clothed and in which they are incorporated, and in their climates they have men whom they possess in servitude. Hell itself and the leaders they call together are servants to be disposed in things according to their natures. And <unclear>this which</unclear> is said was spoken by the "son of the philosophers": when you wish to draw out any of the aforesaid planetary spirits from any of the climates in the aforesaid days, you should admit them through the effects of each planet in its own proper climate.

When you wish to operate under Saturn, you should do this while the Sun is in Capricorn or the Moon is remaining in Sagittarius. You shall make an image of a <unclear>small</unclear> thing without a face, and wrap it in short black cloths.

## The Fourth Stone

**The fourth** stone is called *haudenebus*; Aristotle said that this stone is excellently composed for taking away the [trouble] of many, and it is valuable for soldiers and men-at-arms; so that if ever in war you send them in—if you send them with their soldiers—their bodies are strengthened more than voices [of the enemy]; and thus, being conspicuous, they are more easily moved <note>possibly meaning they move with greater agility or purpose</note>. This stone is truly white in color, whose composition is such:

->Composition of the Fourth Stone<-

Take four ounces of lead; that is, if you wish, with one ounce of melted white sulfur, and eight ounces of silver; let it be melted and again it will coagulate together into one. Afterward, let you put the lead upon it; into the same, everything is finished together. Having incorporated [the lead], season it with the stone *almaziotis*, diamond, four ounces of native sulfur, and two ounces of red copper <note>original: "aes per rubium"</note>; let all be pulverized together; cast the powder upon those bodies, because all are brightened together. Then, just as it is drawn from the fire and tested, afterward you shall do just as in the third way: as with the water and the marrow, just as you would melt it equally from peppers <note>original: "ex piperis," possibly a reference to a pungent plant extract used as a solvent</note>; now mix it with the eyes <note>the "eyes" or surface bubbles of the liquid</note> and likewise with the gentle marrow, and [place] upon it the blood of a sparrow until the coagulation comes forth. Afterward, indeed, eight [ounces] are taken from the skilled works—sometimes it is not best to use it all—and it receives five ounces of *almaziotis*, one ounce of *vincit* <note>unclear technical term, possibly a binder</note>, one ounce of red *arzonis* <note>possibly arsenic or a red resin like dragon's blood</note>, and five [ounces] of powder; and grind them all together; and [add] the aforementioned marrow from the spores already mentioned, as [required]. And place it upon the fire until the whole melts; then draw it from the fire and let it pass into the mold. That which is in the mold, you shall melt it at the fire for the purpose of three specific bodies; and upon them [add] the marrow already mentioned, little by little, until they drink it all up and everything becomes a [single] possession. Then draw it from the fire and put it into the mold; you will have a stone above the market of spirits <note>original: "supra forum spirituum," perhaps meaning of the highest spiritual value</note>, healthy and equal; thus, you will see that I have worked through everything we said before. Then you shall make two [pieces] with large openings from this form, one in the [sun] form and another in the form for soldiers.

# The Third Stone

### Composition of the Third Stone

# The Fourth Stone

The fourth stone is finally called the "elixir," and Aristotle says that this stone is subtly composed for the removal of all wounds. It is of value to knights and men-at-arms, because when they cast themselves into war, if they find themselves among their women <note>meaning in the company of women or thinking of home</note>, their bodies are offered up as weaker; but if they possess this, they will be easily sustained. This stone is indeed white in color, and its composition is as follows:

### Composition of the Fourth Stone

Take four drachms of lead, one drachm each of the flowers of yellow copper and white melted [copper], and half a drachm of silver. Let the silver and the flowers be melted together; afterward, let them be added upon the aforesaid lead. When all have been incorporated together, take the stone of almagra, the diamond of the yellow dew (four drachms), and red silver (two drachms). Let all be pulverized together and added upon the bodies during the process of powdering until they all boil together. Then move it far from the fire and let it rest. Afterward, you shall make it in this way: take the fat <note>original: "sepu," sebum</note> of *alguzel* <note>possibly "al-ghazal," referring to a specific plant or a gazelle</note>, the marrow of *sino* <note>unclear; perhaps a specific bone or plant</note>, and dew—an equal part of each. Let them be melted separately; let them be mixed so that all the marrow is reverberated; and add the soap with sparrow's blood until it begins to coagulate. Afterward, take one drachm of pig bones—not the best, sometimes they are like atoms—and half a drachm of almagra, one drachm of yellow sulfur of the dew, and one and a half drachms of red silver. Let them be pulverized and grind everything together; and the aforesaid marrow and fat already mentioned shall be added. Let it be placed upon the fire until the whole is melted. Then move it from the fire and allow it to solidify. Once solidified, place the bodies from the crucible upon the fire to melt them, and upon them pour the medicine already mentioned little by little until they drink up the whole; and let them all become red. Then move it from the fire and let it solidify. Let it become a stone that is serene, healthy, and equal. After this, you should work through everything we told you before. Then you shall make two large [figures]: one in the form of a man and the other in the form of a woman.

## Chapter five shows which are the 10 sciences necessary for this art, and how this science is drawn from them, and what is the root of the science of necromancy <term>nigromancie: though literally "necromancy," in this medieval context it refers to the high ritual magic of commanding spirits and planetary forces</term>.

# Certain ancient sages, who were more intent on discovering this skill, arrived at what they desired to reach through much labor and the highest inquiry—proving it more through sleeping than through waking—yet they responded through the arts, studying the **ways** of reasoning through intelligence. There follows "gremotica" <note>likely a corruption of *geometria* (geometry)</note>. And after this follows astronomy, through which the paths of the planets and the signs of the stars are known. After this is **music** <note>original: "musonem"; referring to the harmony of the spheres</note>, concerning the **movements** of the **bodies** above, under what **measure** the **fear** of such things is comprehended. After this is dialectic <note>logic and formal reasoning</note>, which is divided into eight books, in which it is written that the wise man enters [the knowledge of] God. After this is physics <note>natural philosophy and medicine</note>, which is divided by the day into two parts, namely the art of governing nature, which **architects** and the **composition** of things have; in these, many books of the ancients are held, through which many things are divined and understood. For there are two natural sciences: one of growth, and the book of the heavens in the world (139 books), and truly there are those books of signs which appear in the [...] a book of souls (69 books), a book of vegetables, a book of [...] from one place to another. Then follows metaphysics, insofar as it exists in 13 books of composition, each of which uses a **good** **intellectual** and **infinite** **power**, the completion of wisdom, and the perfection of the appetite to **reach** [truth]. After all these is this science, which is **said** to be [drawn] from the **ten** **stated** **arts**, although it is recovered [separately]. For those who **anciently** established the same [goal] through these arts, can [attain] power, since it is the **dwelling** of a most **dark** **house**, so that they may be **measured** and **ascend** to all the superior things of the aforementioned **sciences**. Because [this art] **profits** one, it shows how to reach those things which the ancient sages reached. Understand wisdom itself, and know finally how to do those things which they themselves did. # Concerning the Virtues of Stones and Plants

The stone called **aracas**, as it is said, which when not prepared is a stone that is less easily broken, exists in both large and small sizes. In bouts of drunkenness, the one drinking it will immediately lose his intoxicated state.

The **magnet stone** <term>magnetis; magnetite or lodestone</term> of red attraction <note>While magnetite is usually black/grey, "red magnet" may refer to a specific ore or a hematite-rich variety.</note>, if you find one leading another, and if you place it upright on iron, it is drawn to it just as if the iron were being drawn from its own veins. Certain things respond to iron as if a man were leading another. <meta>This page continues the technical instructions for the Twenty-Eight Mansions of the Moon, an astrological system used to time the creation of talismans. This section covers mansions eight through fourteen, focusing on charms for victory, health, social favor, and the manipulation of relationships.</meta>

# The Eighth
mansion is **Annathra** <note>original: "annathra"; the eighth lunar mansion, Al-Nathra, located in the constellation Cancer</note> and it is for **increasing victory**. When the Moon has traveled through this mansion, you should make an image in metal of a man making water <note>original: "aqua facientē hominē"; possibly a figure pouring water or a fountain-like figure</note>, and on the foot, you shall write the name of the lord of this mansion, which can never be healthfully resisted; and likewise, in the same <unclear>pillar</unclear> <note>original: "amudiae"; possibly referring to a column or support of the figure</note>, you shall make the name in such a way and then complete everything in this manner. When you have made this image in this way, you shall place it in the earth before whomever you wish, and you will obtain your way through the help of the lord and the name of the lord of the mansion itself.

# The Ninth
mansion is **Atarcha** <note>original: "atarcha"; the ninth mansion, Al-Tarf, spanning the end of Cancer and start of Leo</note> and it is for **causing infirmity**. When the Moon has traveled through this mansion, you should make a form of a man out of lead, distinct and <unclear>rough</unclear>, holding his hands over his eyes. On his face, you shall write the name of the mansion, a name which cannot be sustained without <term>fumigations</term> <note>the practice of passing an object through the smoke of specific incense to consecrate it</note> and prayers. If there was such a woods [nearby], and then in that same infirmity or from that place, you shall cause blood to go out; and this is said to be for two people: whatever he seeks shall be fulfilled, and everything you wish will be done. You shall write the name then... let him write above the said "Tenas" and the name through "Lambet" <note>likely the names of the presiding spirits of the mansion</note> and the name of the lord of this mansion.

# The Tenth
mansion is **Algetha** <note>original: "algetha"; the tenth mansion, Al-Jabhah, in the constellation Leo</note> and it is for **healing the sick** and for **removing the fear of women**. When the Moon has truly moved through this mansion, you shall make in gold or in coral the form of a lion's head. Above everything, you shall write the name of the lord of the mansion, and then you shall fumigate it and say:

And blood of a black fox 3.4. blood of a black dog / blood of a head
3.1.

<summary>This page lists several pharmacological or alchemical recipes utilizing the blood of various animals (fox, mouse, owl, bear, and black-furred animals) to treat "ill will" and balance bodily humors. The text suggests these preparations could heal hatred and influence a person's disposition.</summary>
